title: Actual object-free body canonical-byte parity
question: Can object-free native body JSON avoid recursive canonicalization while preserving the existing canonical bytes?
method: Within a rollback-only stage read, compare the current native function and quoted-string-preserving whitespace compaction on the actual retained successful-control body. Check independent escaped/Unicode/scalar/array controls and retain object-bearing fallback cases. Compare lengths and SHA-256 digests without returning body text.
conclusion: On 2026-11-19 the actual 23,241,498-byte JSONB body contained no objects. Both paths produced 21,875,525 canonical bytes with SHA-256 136bafe6391ec099e94a357da17ac44e745f5ef3cfffa48bc64538966817b629. Independent controls preserved quoted whitespace, escaped quotes/backslashes and Unicode. The paired length/digest projection took 32.958 seconds through recursion and 2.198 seconds through compaction during another capture. This supported the coordinator’s separately authored N36 repair; this probe changed no installed function or workload deadline.
